title: Full performance-counter <-> 12 FPS benchmark-frame correlation + click markers
requirement: LBA-REQ-011 (extended: all performance counters, not only CPU/RAM/disk)
summary: Correlate EVERY sampled Windows performance counter (not just CPU/RAM/disk) to the 12 FPS benchmark-frame timeline on the shared epoch-ms / frame axis, and let a click on the raw-data chart write a MARKER label into the metadata so post-processing can grab the captured image at that instant within a +/-200 ms tolerance.

frame.note: 12 frames/sec => 1000/12 = 83.333.. ms per frame. frameIndex(epochMs) = floor((epochMs - epochMsAtFrameZero) / frameIntervalMs); null before frame 0 (never clamped).
frame.sharedAxis: epochMs (host clock). Guest samples are shifted onto the host axis via hostGuestOffsetMs before frameIndex resolution.

sampling.note: Counters are sampled ~10 Hz (100 ms) so each 83.33 ms frame has ~1 sample; a frame's counters are the last sample at or before the frame instant, or the mean of samples inside the frame window. Rate counters (…/sec) are already per-second; gauges are instantaneous.

scopeInstances.process: LabVIEW (the launched IDE process; matched by image name, de-duplicated across PIDs by the harness)
scopeInstances.system: _Total instances for Processor/PhysicalDisk; * aggregated for Network Interface / GPU Engine

processor.desc: Total processor busy time (kept as the legacy cpuPct).
Threads waiting for a processor (saturation signal).

memory.desc: LabVIEW private working set (kept as the legacy ramMb).
Hard page faults to/from disk (memory pressure).

disk.desc: Disk busy time (kept as the legacy diskPct).

process.desc: LabVIEW CPU share (can exceed 100 on multi-core).

gpu.desc: Aggregate GPU engine utilization (Windows 10+; present when a GPU counter set exists).

catalogPolicy.note: This is the curated benchmark-relevant superset across processor/memory/disk/network/process/system/GPU. It is NOT the full Windows PDH registry (hundreds of objects); the schema is EXTENSIBLE -- any additional PDH counter path may be added as a {key,pdh,unit,kind,scope} entry and it flows through correlation + markers unchanged. Counters absent on a given host (e.g. no GPU counter set) sample as null and are skipped in window summaries.
catalogPolicy.backwardCompatible: cpuPct/ramMb/diskPct remain valid legacy sample keys, aliased to cpuTotalPct/ramProcessWorkingSetMb/diskTotalPct.

sample.description: One resource sample on the shared epoch-ms axis. Every catalog key MAY appear; a missing/unsupported counter is null (skipped in summaries).

markers.description: Click-to-label on the raw-data chart. A pointer click at chart x-position resolves to an epoch-ms instant; that writes a MARKER into the launch metadata. Post-processing reads markers[] and, for each, grabs the captured frame image whose capture instant is nearest the marker within toleranceMs; outside the tolerance the grab is NOT admitted (no wrong-frame image is attached).

trigger.event: pointer click (mousedown->mouseup without drag) on the metric chart or the frame-correlator scrub track
trigger.resolves: chart x -> epochMs on the shared axis (the same axis the time cursor uses)
trigger.note: Distinguished from a scrub DRAG: a click (movement < clickSlopPx, default 4) creates a marker; a drag moves the time cursor. A modifier (e.g. Alt+click) MAY be used to force-mark.

marker.epochMs: number — click instant on the shared axis
marker.label: string — operator-supplied (prompt) or auto ('marker N')
marker.createdAt: string — ISO-8601 when the click happened

imageGrab.nearestFrameIndex: integer|null — the frame whose captureEpochMs is closest to epochMs
imageGrab.admitted: boolean — deltaMs != null AND deltaMs <= toleranceMs; only then is the frame image grabbed for this marker
imageGrab.imageRef: string|null — path/handle of the grabbed frame image when admitted, else null

markers.postProcessing: For each marker: find argmin over frames of |captureEpochMs(frame) - marker.epochMs|; if that min <= 200 ms, attach frame.image as the marker image (admitted=true); otherwise admitted=false and no image is attached. This keeps a marker's image honest to +/-200 ms of the clicked instant.

correlationOutputPreserved.note: The v1 pre/post-trigger window analysis is preserved and now runs PER catalog key (not only cpu/ram/disk): each key gets {pre:{count,mean,min,max}, post:{count,mean,min,max}, deltaMean}. triggerFrameIndex, hostGuestOffsetMs, sample/pre/post counts are unchanged.
